title: Airports
summary: Airports (May Subd Geog) is used for collective works on the airports serving a city or region. Individual airports are entered under their corporate names; works on an airport's physical plant also get [city]--Buildings, structures, etc. for the major city or cities served.
validation_rules: `Airports` may be subdivided geographically (May Subd Geog) and is used for works discussing collectively the airports, airfields, etc., serving a city or region, e.g. `Airports--Washington Metropolitan Area`. (H 1211 sec. 1)
An individual airport is entered as a corporate name heading (610), e.g. `Heathrow Airport`, not as `Airports--[place]`. (H 1211 sec. 2)
For works on an airport's physical plant (terminal buildings, runways, etc.), also assign `[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.` for the major city or cities the airport serves. (H 1211 sec. 2)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Airports* (May Subd Geog) to works that discuss collectively the airports, airfields, etc., that serve the city or region. Example:

```
Title:  Air facilities, 1967, Washington metropolitan area.
650 #0 $a Airports $z Washington Metropolitan Area.
```

sections.heading: 2. Individual airports
sections.text:
To works that discuss a specific airport, assign the corporate name heading for the individual airport. If the work discusses the physical plant of the airport, including the terminal building(s), runways, etc., also assign the heading *[city]--Buildings, structures, etc.* for the major city (or cities) that the airport serves. Examples:

```
Title:  Gateway to the world : the illustrated story of the London Airport.
610 20 $a Heathrow Airport.
651 #0 $a London (England) $x Buildings, structures, etc.

Title:  A giant in Texas : a history of the Dallas-Fort Worth Regional Airport controversy, 1911-1974.
610 20 $a Dallas-Fort Worth Regional Airport $x History.
651 #0 $a Dallas (Tex.) $x Buildings, structures, etc. $x History.
651 #0 $a Fort Worth (Tex.) $x Buildings, structures, etc. $x History.
```
